blocks.text: JavaScript Datatypes
JavaScript has 8 Datatypes
A JavaScript variable can hold 8 types of data:

rows: A text of characters enclosed in quotes
A number representing a mathematical value
A number representing a large integer
A data type representing true or false
A collection of key-value pairs of data
A primitive variable with no assigned value
A primitive value representing object absence

blocks.caption: Examples

blocks.text: The typeof Operator

You can use the JavaScript typeof operator to find the type
of a JavaScript variable.
The typeof operator returns the type of a variable or an expression:

typeof ""             // Returns
 "string"

typeof "John"         // Returns
 "string"

typeof "John Doe"     // Returns
 "string"
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
typeof 0              // Returns
 "number"

  typeof 314            // Returns
 "number"

  typeof 3.14           // Returns
 "number"

  typeof (3)            // Returns
 "number"
typeof (3 + 4)        // Returns
 "number"
blocks.caption: Example

Datatype undefined

In computer programs, variables are often declared without a value. The value
can be something that has to be calculated, or something that will be provided
later, like user input.
A variable without a value has the datatype undefined.
A variable without a value also has the value undefined.
let carName;

blocks.text: Empty Values
An empty value has nothing to do with undefined.
An empty string has both a legal value and a type.

let car = "";    //
    The value is
    "", the typeof is "string"
